subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When the Codex native relay cannot be invoked, should OpenClaw preserve fail-closed native approval semantics while repairing the relay, or intentionally permit generic before-tool policy fallback?
rationale: The two paths are not demonstrably equivalent for invocation failures, trusted-policy handling, approval prompts, or handler errors; accepting fallback is a security-boundary decision rather than a routine implementation detail.

options.title: Repair relay and remain fail-closed
options.body: Use current main’s lifecycle/generation recovery, recreate or refresh missing relay state, and allow fallback only for a narrowly proven pre-invocation unavailable state.

options.title: Accept generic policy fallback
options.body: Intentionally allow generic before-tool evaluation after recognized relay unavailability, with exact-head live proof covering denials, prompts, trusted policy, and handler failures.

options.title: Close as superseded
options.body: Close this branch if current main’s restart-generation recovery fully resolves the linked report without the additional fallback semantics.

recommendation.title: Repair relay and remain fail-closed
recommendation.body: Use current main’s lifecycle/generation recovery, recreate or refresh missing relay state, and allow fallback only for a narrowly proven pre-invocation unavailable state.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged fallback and restart-generation history places the permanent native approval boundary closest to this owner.
